author: Martin Pegan
description:
• Former Test opener says object also used on cricket ball in Port Elizabeth

  • CA remains ‘comfortable’ with bans only for Bancroft, Warner and Smith

Usman Khawaja has claimed “all” of the Australia touring party knew about the plot to tamper with the ball against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018 and the team also used sandpaper during the second Test at Port Elizabeth.

The former Australia batter said the team used sandpaper to tamper with the ball before Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera while handling the object during the third Test, ahead of the release of Khawaja’s autobiography Sabr on Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It was all of us’: Khawaja says entire Australia team knew about sandpaper ball tampering plot

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Elliot English died on Friday from injuries sustained in fire in Waterford that also claimed lives of his parents

A six-year-old boy has become the third child in his family to die after a suspected arson attack in Waterford that also claimed the lives of his parents, police have said.

Elliot English died on Friday at Children’s Health Ireland hospital in Crumlin from injuries sustained in the 13 October fire in Birchwood, Ireland.

Continue reading...
title: Boy, six, third child in his family to die after suspected arson attack in Ireland

author: Brendan Fanning at the Aviva Stadium
description:
• Ireland 42-12 Argentina

  • Carreras scores twice in Nations Championship defeat

If taking each game as it comes is the North Star for every sportsman then it wasn’t easily visible approaching this opener to November’s international window. There has never been a time when Ireland and Argentina liked each other. Not in the era when their collisions were uncapped affairs – by Ireland – and certainly not when they were upgraded to full Test status. Mean and nasty World Cup meetings were sources of spice. But this was almost tame.

Next year’s World Cup in Australia provided the backdrop to this, with a decent chance of this pair meeting there in the knockout stages. If that comes to pass then Ireland will consider complacency their biggest enemy.

Continue reading...
title: Keenan hat-trick inspires six-try Ireland to emphatic win against Argentina

author: Associated Press
description:
Faculty senate passed resolution expressing deep discontent with school’s response to alleged fraternity rape

Cornell University’s faculty senate approved a resolution on Friday declaring “no confidence” in the school’s top leaders, a symbolic gesture reflecting deep discontent on campus in the wake of a former student’s lawsuit saying she was gang-raped at a fraternity party in 2024.

The resolution passed 75-50, with five faculty senators abstaining and five others not voting, according to an email sent to members of the faculty senate on Friday afternoon.

Continue reading...
title: Cornell faculty declares ‘no confidence’ in school leaders in fallout from alleged gang-rape

author: Johana Bhuiyan
description:
Men allegedly impersonated voices and images of executives to convince employees to send large payments

Three foreign nationals were arrested and charged with using AI to allegedly impersonate corporate CEOs and attorneys to steal over $100m, according to an indictment that was newly unsealed by the US Department of Justice.

According to a press release from the United States attorney’s office for the southern district of New York, three men – Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, and Guy Sheetrit – were arrested for using AI to alter and impersonate the voices and images of executives and attorneys at various companies in order to convince employees to send over large payments. Soall and Hazan were arrested in Spain over the summer, while Sheetrit was arrested in the United Kingdom in September. The alleged fraud took place between 2024 an
title: Three men charged in US with using AI to impersonate CEOs and steal millions

author: Guardian sport and agencies
description:
• Bilka and Edwards score twice each in American rout

  • Canada open with 5-1 win over Sweden as Eldridge shines

  • Jersey dispute overshadows tournament’s Danish debut

The United States opened their defense of the women’s ice hockey world championship with a 7-0 victory over Switzerland on Friday in Esbjerg, Denmark.

Hannah Bilka and Laila Edwards scored twice each, while Kirsten Simms, Hilary Knight and Casey O’Brien also found the net as the Americans pulled away after a competitive opening period. Caroline Harvey contributed three assists.

Continue reading...
title: USA women throttle Switzerland 7-0 to open hockey worlds amid jersey dispute

author: Miles Herbert and Jacqui Housden
description:
The Guardian’s weekend wrap of essential reads from the past seven days, selected by Miles Herbert and Jacqui Housden

  • Get this in your inbox every weekend. Sign up for Five Great Reads here

Hello and welcome to the weekend.

We went big this week. In this selection of reads from across the Guardian, big wins are dissected, big questions are asked, big bowls are taste-tested and dreams of being bigger are realised. Enjoy.

Continue reading...
title: Five Great Reads: What now for Trump, a cruise from hell, and manhood enhancements

author: John Clegg
description:
Art historian, critic and poet who hosted ‘the Group’, a literary workshop of the 1950s and 60s

The poet, art critic and historian Edward Lucie-Smith, who has died aged 93, was both prolific and polymathic. He wrote almost 100 full-length books, including studies of individual artists and large-scale historical surveys, among them The Male Nude: A Modern View (1985), Impressionist Women (1989) and Art and Civilization (1992).

His suspicion of contemporary pieties did not lead him to any quick dismissal of contemporary work; rather, he remained permanently excited by the new, and keen to communicate what he saw in it. In an interview in 2017, he gave his account of what he saw as the value of an art critic: “1. Pointing out what they think is good. 2. Saying why they think it’s good, in terms transparent enough for the audience they are addressing to understand.” His own wo
title: Edward Lucie-Smith obituary

author: Vikram Dodd and Emine Sinmaz
description:
Met police chief says ‘many more’ victims could come forward, as actor and comedian awaits sentencing

Police are bracing themselves for more victims of Russell Brand to come forward with at least 10 more women suspected of being attacked by the disgraced star.

Brand, 51, will be sentenced on Monday to what is expected to be a lengthy jail sentence for rape and sexual assaults after he abused his fame to become a “predator” targeting women, and got away with it for years.

Continue reading...
title: Russell Brand suspected to have attacked at least 10 other women

author: Benjamin Lee
description:
The Chilean film-maker, whose films starred Florence Pugh, Julianne Moore and Rachel Weisz, died at his home in Santiago

Chilean film-maker Sebastián Lelio has died at the age of 52.

He was best known for the Oscar-winning trans drama A Fantastic Woman and his English-language films included Gloria Bell and The Wonder.

Continue reading...
title: Sebastián Lelio, director of A Fantastic Woman and Gloria, dies aged 52

author: Lois Beckett
description:
Officials expected to investigate whether super El Niño storms in US south-west damaged the Alien Throne spires

Undulating, gravity-defying rock spires are one of the most magical parts of the landscape of the US south-west.

But after torrential rainstorms linked to the super El Niño season, at least one famous rock formation in north-west New Mexico has been found in pieces.

Continue reading...
title: Famous New Mexico rock formation destroyed after torrential El Niño rains

author: Robert Kitson
description:
Sunday’s hosts need to stop looking for excuses and focus on what they can control to kick off the Nations Championsip against battle-hardened Australia

Several things are increasingly guaranteed from an English rugby perspective around this time of year. Bang on cue the injury news and the weather both start to worsen. Cracks in the relationship between the players and their head coach, in this case Steve Borthwick, begin to surface. And as the crowds stream up from Twickenham railway station past the biltong and burger stalls, no one has much idea what to expect.

This year it has been the same old story. Particularly on the injury front. If Tom Curry, Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland had not all been hurt on the Bagshot training pitch, all three would probably be in England’s matchday 23. With Guy Pepper, Benhard van Rensburg, Sam Underhill, Kepu Tuipulot
title: Injury crises and Borthwick under scrutiny: it’s that time of year again for England rugby

author: Chloe Mac Donnell
description:
Worn by Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, Andy Burnham and Volodymyr Zelenskyy, fashion experts say the look radiates authority and no-nonsense masculinity

For years the black T-shirt was consigned to the clothing category of plain basics. A hidden layer rather than the main event. But modern politics has pushed it to the frontlines as a sartorial shortcut to signal power.

The progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who this week became the first Muslim elected to the US Senate in history, made a tight black T-shirt his signature look throughout his year-long campaign trail. Styling it with jeans and friendship bracelets made by his children, El-Sayed described his attire as “minimal look, maximal politics”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Minimal look, maximal politics’: how the black T-shirt became a political weapon

author: David Hytner
description:
• Jude had asked head coach to scout Dortmund midfielder

  • ‘It will be beautiful for Jude to have his brother close’

Thomas Tuchel has given a first England call-up to Jobe Bellingham, admitting the midfielder’s older brother, Jude, had nagged him to do so, as he set up the prospect of their family dream being realised.

Tuchel’s inclusion of the younger Bellingham for the Nations League ties against Croatia and Spain was further evidence of his shift away from the squad that served him well at the World Cup last summer and towards a fresh dynamic for the mission to win Euro 2028. The manager has named a 25-man group for the game against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday and the one against Spain in Madrid three days after; of the 22 outfield players, only 11 were at the World Cup.
title: Bellinghams celebrate ‘beautiful story’ as Jobe joins Jude in Tuchel’s England 2.0

author: Exclusive by Matt Hughes
description:
• Concern among counties due to reliance on ECB funding

  • Optimism that eventual figure could be reduced to £35m

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) is forecasting losses of tens of millions of pounds next year despite hosting the Ashes, with county executives told last week that the deficit could be as large as £50m.

The anticipated shortfall, after posting a profit of £12.6m in 2025, is due to a combination of the cyclical nature of the governing body’s media revenues, which is largely determined by domestic opposition, and a recent decision by the International Cricket Council (ICC) to withhold a portion of the broadcast payments owed to members that it had been due to distribute in 2027.

Continue reading...
title: ECB forecasting losses of up to £50m in 2027 despite visit of Australia for the Ashes

author: Matthew Weaver
description:
Harry, Doreen Lawrence, Elton John, David Furnish, Elizabeth Hurley and Sadie Frost face £50m bill after ruling

Prince Harry and five other prominent figures have launched a legal challenge against a judge’s verdict in their unsuccessful claims against the Daily Mail publisher Associated Newspapers.

Harry, Doreen Lawrence, the mother of the murdered black teenager Stephen Lawrence, the singer Elton John and his husband, David Furnish, and the actors Elizabeth Hurley and Sadie Frost faced a legal bill of more than £50m after losing their case claiming that Mail journalists used unlawful methods to source stories.

Continue reading...
title: Prince Harry and others launch appeal after losing Daily Mail phone-hacking claim

author: Adria R Walker in Jackson, Mississippi
description:
Democratic and Republican lawyers and groups trade sharp legal letters about procedures for counting ballots in tight race

  • Where Trump and Republicans lost the midterms – a visual analysis of the key states

Democrat Scott Colom is on the verge of winning a Senate seat in Mississippi in a stunning upset, but ballots are still being counted in a close race where Colom holds a lead of just under 2,000 votes over Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. Losing ruby-red Mississippi would be the final straw for Republicans after a midterm sweep by Democrats that turned Texas and South Carolina blue.

A possible legal fight is also
title: Lawyers descend on Mississippi as vote counting continues in razor-thin Senate race

author: Ajit Niranjan
description:
Separate actions also take place outside fence and across Europe in backlash against impact of AI boom

Activists have stormed the site of a Microsoft datacentre being built in Amsterdam, as the backlash to the social and environmental harms of the AI boom spreads across Europe.

Protesters from Geef Tegengas, a Dutch direct action group, clashed with police while breaking into a construction site at Westpoort Amsterdam, where some members climbed a crane, lit flares and tied helium balloons to equipment.

Continue reading...
title: Activists break into building site of Microsoft datacentre in Amsterdam

author: Scott Murray
description:
⚽ Premier League updates from the 8pm GMT kick-off
⚽ Today’s Football Daily | Live scores | Table | Mail Scott

If Everton win this match tonight, they go above Liverpool; if they win it big – five goals big – they leap over Chelsea into fourth spot. Things are going pretty well for David Moyes and his men, who are outperforming expectations that were set miserably low after an underwhelming transfer window. It’s one heck of a turnaround.

But then Coventry City will be pretty pleased with their efforts so far too. After a cold start, they’ve won three of their last five matches, and while nine points and 16th place isn’t exactly the m
title: Everton v Coventry City: Premier League – live

author: Editorial
description:
The tech sell-off exposes fragile promises, while Democratic victories offer a chance to protect workers and hold firms accountable

This week’s midterms showed that the political bill for the AI boom is falling due. The Democratic sweep intensified fears over runaway spending, mounting debt and resistance to datacentres, sending tech shares tumbling. On Thursday Wall Street suffered its worst day since the pandemic as $3.2tn was wiped from markets. Anthropic, developer of the Claude chatbot, is hoping to float within the next fortnight for $1.5tn (£1.1tn), but it may not now get even a trillion dollars. The dominant AI chipmaker
title: The Guardian view on the AI backlash: American voters want a say in their future | Editorial

author: Editorial
description:
The brave women who testified against the star have struck a blow against the sexual entitlement that he personified

The conviction of Russell Brand for one rape and three sexual assaults on Thursday would never have happened were it not for the remarkable courage of his victims. There was no guarantee, before the trial, that he would be found guilty; two more rape charges and one of attempted indecent assault ended in acquittal. The women who testified about what Brand did to them between 2004 and 2009 are owed a debt of gratitude by everyone who believes that sexual predators should pay a price for their crimes, even when they are celebrities. On Monday, Brand will receive what the judge said would be a “significant” jail sentence.</
title: The Guardian view on Russell Brand: his conviction sends a powerful message | Editorial

author: Guardian staff
description:
Democrats have taken control of Congress in a sweeping blue wave. Our reporters answer your questions about the results of the midterm elections

  • Live results from the US midterm elections

Grauniad9999 asks in the comments: With the Democrat Senate majority and the likelihood of Maga / Republican splintering, what is the odds of achieving impeachment numbers in the Senate?

Lauren Gambino, senior political correspondent: I think it would very much depend on who was being impeached. There is a lot of anger at the defense Sec. Hegseth. And we could have an early test of who might be willing to side with Democrats on an impeachment if Congressma
title: What happens after the ‘blue wave’? Our team answers your midterm election results question

author: Giles Richards
description:
The Scuderia are hopeful of being in the world championship mix next season but risk puncturing their chances if they can’t corral their men in the cockpits

Going into this weekend’s São Paulo Grand Prix, all indications are that the status quo at Ferrari will no longer suffice for Lewis Hamilton if the Scuderia’s ambition to return their first drivers’ F1 championship since 2007 is to be taken seriously.

This year’s drivers’ title is already decided with Kimi Antonelli triumphant at the last round in Mexico and Ferrari are already looking toward next season where they are hopeful of genuinely being in the mix against the Italian and Mercedes.

Continue reading...
title: Hamilton v Leclerc: how can Ferrari solve problem of two number one drivers?

author: Chloe Mac Donnell Deputy fashion and lifestyle editor
description:
Fashion house move marks breakthrough in white, male-dominated industry

For the first time in its 109-year history, the fashion house Balenciaga is to be led by a woman, with the British designer Martine Rose appointed as creative director of the brand.

Her appointment at Balenciaga marks a breakthrough in the white, male-dominated fashion industry. Rose is only the second Black woman to lead a major European house. Her appointment follows Grace Wales Bonner, who in 2025 was announced as the men’s creative director at Hermès.

Continue reading...
title: Martine Rose appointed creative director at Balenciaga

author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
description:
After Thursday’s share price plunge on Wall Street, could the volatility be the start of a huge market meltdown?

  • Business live – latest updates

Global financial markets have been thrown into a tailspin as investors bet on an AI slowdown after the US midterm elections.

This is not the first time stock markets have wobbled in recent months due to concerns over a tech bubble. But could this volatility be the start of a huge market meltdown?

Continue reading...
title: US tech stock rout: is the AI bubble bursting?

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
Markle, 82, was taken into custody near Tampa, according to news wires from AP and Reuters, citing unnamed sources

Thomas Markle, the father of Prince Harry’s wife Meghan Markle, has been arrested by US federal agents in Florida on charges related to child sexual abuse material, according to federal law enforcement sources.

Markle, 82, was taken into custody near Tampa, according to news wires from the Associated Press and Reuters, citing unnamed sources. The Duchess of Sussex said last month that she was “deeply distressed” about allegations that a collection of child sexual abuse images was found at her father’s former home.
title: Meghan Markle’s father arrested in Florida on charges related to child sexual abuse material – reports

author: Stephanie Gravalese
description:
Juneau has little arable land, a short growing season and few farmers – and deep traditions of residents and the land feeding each other

Forty miles north-west of Alaska’s capital, the highway just ends.

At Glacier Highway’s most northern point, the pavement turns to gravel, the gravel widens into a turnaround and the tire tracks curve back the way they came. At the far end, the woods begin, a narrow hiking trail slipping toward the southern end of Berners Bay.

Continue reading...
title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing

author: Éva Malpass
description:
Are you one of 600 million people with lower back pain? Osteopaths identify the most common causes – and remedies

Was jet-washing the patio the straw that broke the camel’s – and your – back? That’s a possibility, but experts say the actual causes of back pain may surprise you – and it’s a bigger issue than most may realise. The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that lower back pain is the leading cause of disability worldwide, with cases projected to rise to more than 800 million by 2050, largely as populations grow and age. Here, clinicians reveal some of the unexpected causes, and how to avoid them.

Continue reading...
title: Experts on why your back hurts – and what to do about it

author: Nathan Law
description:
My friend Joshua Wong was due to be released next January. Under draconian security laws, his sentence has been extended by 10 years

Two years ago, I wrote in this newspaper about the lengthy imprisonment of my friend Joshua Wong, who I spent years campaigning alongside for the advancement of Hong Kong’s democracy. He was given an unjust sentence meant to keep him behind bars until January 2027. He was supposed to be released in a few months, when I hoped he would finally be able to reunite with his friends and family and embark on a new chapter.

But this hope was misplaced. The end of the tunnel isn’t next year; it’s late 2036. By then, he will be 40. On Thursday, Joshua was sentenced to another 10 years under Hong Kong’s nation
title: Hong Kong’s prisoners are China’s signal to the world: there is no hope for democracy on its soil | Nathan Law

author: Michael Cragg
description:
(Virgin)
The reunion that fans were hoping for turns out to be a cash-grab box set – though there is a worthwhile curio featuring Posh on lead vocals

Is there a more taunted fanbase than that of the Spice Girls? Seemingly every other week a story – usually perpetuated by Mel B, the band’s number one cheerleader – appears in the tabloids hinting at some sort of reunion. Or film. Or documentary. Swift denials then emerge, typically linked to Geri or Victoria, and all is calm until a week or so later.

So when teasers showing landmarks from 1996’s Wannabe video suddenly appeared on the band’s official social media accounts in September, it felt as if the fans had something tangible to celebrate. The comments quickly filled with hopes of another reunion tour following 2007’s full-band jaunt and 2019’s Posh-less stadium trek. In a music landscape littered with nostalgia tours, surely Ginger, Scary, Baby, Sporty and (maybe) Posh could strap on some Buffalo
title: Spice Girls: The Singles Collection review – stop fleecing your fans right now, thank you very much

author: Jesse Hassenger
description:
The SNL alum has an appealing energy and this is an improvement on the 2003 travesty but it’s also far too long and strangely corporate

Over a long enough timeline, perhaps every living alumnus of Saturday Night Live will play the Cat in the Hat. Mike Myers kicked off this unexpected tradition by embodying the furry, anarchic Dr Seuss character for a notoriously, almost defiantly ghastly 2003 live-action treatment. After doing us all the service of killing flesh-and-blood Seuss movies for good, Myers was later followed by a more charming Martin Short (via voiceover on a cute PBS/CBC animated series) and now Bill Hader, stepping into the role for a big-budget animated reboot from the oft-flailing animation division of Warner Bros.

Just to be clear, this is the same studio that passed on releasing not one but two well-liked features starring their trademark Looney Tunes characters in the last few years. (Puzzlingly, a new Looney Tunes short starring Daffy Duck nonetheless
title: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess

The Guardian’s picture editors select photographs from around the world

author: Owen Lewis
description:
The Warriors’ freshman has spent his first weeks in the NBA antagonizing superstars, speaking his mind and emerging as one of the league’s most compelling personalities

If a screen-addled pickup basketball player teleported into the body of a high-level athlete, they might resemble Yaxel Lendeborg. The most commonly cited fact about Lendeborg is that he used to spend 12 to 14 hours a day gaming, and didn’t debut on his high school basketball team until he was an upperclassman. Professional athletes often have origin stories that resemble the superhero more than the mortal, but Lendeborg really was just like us at one point. Lendeborg has also said that prior to entering the NBA, he didn’t really watch it, either. The Puerto Rican forward racked up more than enough accolades in college to qualify for the NBA, including helming Michigan
title: Yaxel Lendeborg is the NBA’s most entertaining rookie – and he’s not holding back

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Decision made in order for factory in Texas to be used for Cybercab, the carmaker’s self-driving taxi

Elon Musk has announced that Tesla will wind down production of its Cybertruck, marking the end of a failed effort to take a chunk of the lucrative market for pickups in the US.

The billionaire chief executive said production of the car will stop in about the middle of next year at the company’s factory in Texas in order to use the plant for the Cybercab, its self-driving taxi.

Continue reading...
title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production as Elon Musk focuses on robotics and AI

description:
Have you followed the big stories in football, rugby league, tennis, cricket, rugby union, Formula One and athletics?

author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent
description:
YouGov survey finds support for tree planting and emissions taxes but opposition to air travel and fuel levies

  • Europe live – latest updates

Europeans believe human-made climate change is real, a survey has shown, with most feeling action must be taken soon – as long as they do not have to sacrifice too much to achieve it.

The YouGov poll of six European countries showed between 69% (Germany) and 80% (France) of respondents believed the climate was changing, with few (1%-4%) denying it and 14-20% believing it was changing, but not as a result of human activity.

Continue reading...
title: Most Europeans want action to tackle climate crisis but not at any cost, poll shows

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Cabin upgrade is move to offer wealthy passengers greater luxury as airlines compete for their business

  • Business live – latest updates

Singapore Airlines has said it will offer the “largest double bed in the sky” as part of a S$2bn (£1.2bn) cabin upgrade as super-rich passengers demand ever greater levels of luxury travel.

The first-class premium cabins will feature what the airline claims is “the largest double bed in commercial aviation”.

Continue reading...
title: Dream ticket? Super-rich can sleep pretty with Singapore Airlines ‘largest double bed in the sky’

author: Matt Mills and Ben Beaumont-Thomas
description:
Inspired by everything from Radiohead to Deerhoof and Linda Perhacs, the west country band merge disparate styles into solid anthems

From Bristol, UK
Recommended if you like Puscifer, Julie Christmas, the Mars Volta
Up next Supporting Every Hell at Bristol’s Exchange, 4 December; playing UK festivals Strangeforms, Noizzefest and Arctangent in 2027

Even a cursory scroll through Sans Froid’s influences will make you expect chaos. In interviews, members of the west country rockers have acknowledged Radiohead, the Mars Volta, the immersive folk of Linda Perhacs and even the haywire opera/metal/breakbeat of French button-pusher Igorrr. Combine that array with the four-piece’s sole collective inspiration – San Franciscan indie experimentalists Deerhoof – and it’s amazing there’s any coherence at all.
title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: crowd-pleasing anticapitalist rockers Sans Froid

author: Roque Planas
description:
Wildlife advocates incensed as documents show state paid out $2,000 per kill in effort to shrink state’s wolf population

Idaho officials paid hunters thousands of dollars for killing a dozen newborn wolf pups this spring, including what appears to be at least one full litter killed in or near its den, according to state records shared with the Guardian and Public Domain.

The wolf pup killings have incensed wildlife advocates in Idaho, where state wildlife officials have been ordered to take extraordinary measures to shrink the state’s re-introduced wolf population amid complaints from the livestock industry and big game hunting outfitters.

Continue reading...
title: ‘An abomination’: Idaho hunters earned thousands of dollars to kill newborn wolf pups, records reveal

author: Deepa Parent
description:
While some fear another full-scale war, others are less sure – but both agree repression at home will continue

Just hours after the US midterm election results delivered a crushing defeat for the Republican party, pro-regime crowds gathered in Tehran’s Enghelab Square to set fire to a giant banner depicting Donald Trump, his vice-president, JD Vance, the US envoy Steve Witkoff and the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

Iranian officials have since issued defiant statements celebrating the Republican losses, portraying the results as a rejection of Trump’s war against Iran.

Continue reading...
title: ‘We’ve been preparing for the worst all year’: uncertainty grips Iran after Trump midterms defeat

author: Michelle R Smith
description:
Meta says it removes content that could cause imminent physical harm – but nearly half a million members have joined a group that regularly promotes misinformation

As a measles outbreak spread through Lancaster county, Pennsylvania, in August, a parent turned to a massive public Facebook group, Crunchy Moms, for advice. They were considering getting their three-year-old vaccinated, in part to protect their six-month-old.

“I’m nervous for my baby,” the parent wrote.

Continue reading...
title: Measles, mumps and misinformation: how Crunchy Moms became ‘the most dangerous’ group on Facebook

author: Sandeep Parmar
description:
The Universe is an Animal by Jessica Mookherjee; Sleep Gate by Sylvia Legris; The Other Love by Henri Cole; Stay Winter by Nidhi Zak/Aria Eipe

The Universe Is an Animal by Jessica Mookherjee (Nine Arches, £11.99)
In this confident and capacious collection, scientific language commingles with familial histories of displacement and war. Echoes of violence, from the partition of East Pakistan and India, now modern-day Bangladesh, to an arrival in Wales, haunt many of the poems. In Waterlily, Mookherjee inverts Monet’s signature image into something far more sinister. An aunt “hides under Bhatiyari Lake, sari billows / until the men leave” to escape communal riots. Longer poems, such as this one, encode repetition and refrain into a genetic pattern of sound and meaning: “the dress she sews me is washed
title: The best recent poetry – review roundup

author: Jonathan Freedland
description:
Yes, the Republicans suffered humiliating defeat. But the fact that a Trump presidency was even possible means something like it could happen again

He’s down, but not quite out. Barring divine or other intervention, Donald Trump will remain in the Oval Office for a further two years and 10 weeks. Or, as the White House put it in a plaintive social media post brimming with neediness: “PSA [Public Service Announcement]: Trump is still your president.” But that’s not the only reason why the global celebrations that greeted the Democratic tidal wave that swept Republicans out of even their deepest heartlands should be tempered, if only a tad.

Don’t get me wrong, the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections are cause for genuine international jubilation. The defeats of Trump allies in Serbia and Brazil w
title: After the midterms, the global right is reeling. But the danger of Trumpism will never be gone | Jonathan Freedland

author: Tom Bassam (now) and David Tindall (earlier)
description:
⚽ All the latest heading into a busy weekend of football
⚽ Premier League: 10 things to look out for | Mail David

What do we make of that then? Josh King a better player than Cole Palmer? Looks like this goes beyond just playing ability. Tuchel’s press conference is set for 11am so we’ll see how he explains what looks like a huge snub.

The other big news in Tuchel’s squad announcement is that there is again no place for Cole Palmer. Other surprise omissions include Noni Madueke and Kobbie Mainoo.

Continue reading...
title: Jobe Bellingham called up by England, Sunderland face jeers and the FA Cup first round: football news – live

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Prime minister said his government would bring in legal requirement for companies to say what they pay when listing new jobs

Palantir’s controversial £330m health contract is to be extended before ministers draw up plans to replace it with a British alternative, the FT has reported.

Health secretary Yvette Cooper has faced calls from MPs and campaigners to axe the US tech firm’s contract to deliver the flagship government AI system.

The reports today that Labour is to keep Palantir in the NHS shows that the huge sums of money paid to the likes of former Labour ministers, Peter Mandelson and Tom Watson, looks to have paid off.

Any evidence of patient benefit is highly contested by NHS staff and many NHS trusts have rejected the use of Palantir’s platform.

The benefits of smart glasses must be weighed against the harms they can cause. The government is already looking into options to restrict smart glasses in certain settings and restric
title: Burnham to force employers to publish salaries on job ads in latest government ‘small fix’ – UK politics live

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Hoax bomb threats targeted commercial flights this week leaving at least 35 planes searched or diverted

A Romanian airline Tarom flight from Prague to Bucharest is the latest believed to be affected by today’s bomb threats.

The aircraft, operating flight number ROT226M, sent a squawk code of 7700 – general emergency – before landing safely in Bucharest. The threat was later confirmed to be unproven.

Once this tasty tuber is established in your garden, you’ll have a crop for life. Great news – if you can digest them

It’s intriguingly rare to see a crop of jerusalem artichokes, considering how easy they are to grow. They’re part of the sunflower family and, surprisingly, entirely unrelated to the globe artichoke. They produce tall, leggy stems upon which a bright yellow flower blooms, and while they lack the size and sturdiness of sunflowers, they make up for that by appearing in great numbers and developing edible tubers underground. Despite these admirable features, there are good reasons why they are not the most common sight.

First, though nutty and delicious, these tubers can be quite hard to digest – earning them the nickname “fartichokes”. They contain a carbohydrate that can be tough on the gut, so it’s recommended that they are cooked well and introduced into y

Just 16 games into the year, McDavid has 31 assists. It’s the fastest anyone has ever hit that milestone in any NHL season. description:
The Indian-Irish poet on the Mahabharata retelling that inspired her to write, Arundhati Roy’s courage, and the poetry of Lucille Clifton

My earliest reading memory
My father was a sailor and my mother a teacher. They were both voracious readers. I was lucky enough to come from a home full of books and when we joined my father out at sea for extended periods of time, my mother carried plenty of books for me to read. I remember sitting by the porthole in our cabin, looking out at the sea on a sunny day, the ship moving calmly through the waters. I was reading The Tale of Peter Rabbit by Beatrix Potter, a book that still feels like a dream. I was four years old.

My favourite book growing up
There were so many, but when I was a child experiencing the death of my great-grandmother, a maternal figure who I adored, The Neverending Story by Michael Ende became the most essential read for me.

author: Anjul Behal in Panipat. Photographs by Elke Scholiers
description:
In Panipat, 1m tons of used clothing a year are turned into products for global brands, but dangerous machinery and few safeguards mean life-changing injuries are common

For three months, Suraj Kumar’s job was to feed discarded clothes into shredding machines in Panipat, an industrial city in the north Indian state of Haryana. Clothes discarded in the US, Canada and Europe arrive in the city to be torn back into fibres and spun into yarn, feeding a textile recycling industry that supplies markets across the world.

Suraj, 19, had travelled from West Bengal state to work in Panipat’s factories, following his cousins and friends who had already found jobs there. He hoped to earn enough to send money home to his parents. But in late August, an electrical short circuit in the machine propelled him into the shredding mechanism. The accident crushed both arms.

The veteran travel writer turns his eye for detail on his northern neighbour and its people

Paul Theroux’s arrival in Canada doesn’t go well. An immigration officer called Sweeney finds a small pocketknife in his car and fines him $500 for failing to declare a weapon. “I’m going to make you famous,” he angrily tells her, stumping up. Maybe he will, with this book. Canadians are reputed to be polite and easygoing, “slaves to their courtesy”, but the country has changed enormously in recent years. Will Theroux find it stuffed with Sweeney-ites? Luckily the answer is no.

He issues a warning that, after 11 previous travel books, this may be his last; global overtourism appals him and so does much travel writing. But he shares Jack Kerouac’s delight in being on the road, and from his home in Massachusetts it’s just a four-hour drive to the border. His purpose is less to check out “the strangers next door” than to visit the village of Yamaska, in Quebec. It was ther

In May 1767, a notice was placed in the Manchester Mercury for “Any Gentleman, or Lady, wanting to purchase a Black Boy, 12 years of age” to inquire on Market Street, at the site of today’s Uniqlo clothes shop.

After 15 years of painstaking work through the scattered fragments that recorded and pointed to Manchester’s enslaving history, I still don’t think I have come to terms with my moment of discovery, a few months ago, of those few words captured in black and white. The sale of a human being, a child, on our busiest shopping street.

The Student List has shown my generation, who protested against the Milošević regime in the 1990s, how we should have done it

On Halloween, a few days after a student-led movement swept aside an illiberal, seemingly invincible regime in my native Serbia, I was sitting on the Vienna tram and watched various friendly and malicious monsters getting on and off around me. Witches, devils and unicorns were politely making their way to their respective parties.

Not all monsters wear fancy dress. Later that evening, I walked past a Serbian restaurant; in front of it stood a group of grumpy-looking men. They were smoking, spitting and swearing. I recognised the hardened, couldn’t-care-less attitude, the smell of corruption, the penchant for violence. Yet they looked as though their lives were coming to an end. These men are the losers of the revolution that is taking place in Serbia. Their smuggling routes and deals are under threat. Their criminal networks no longer function.</
title: Serbia has banished the monsters from Belgrade – it was, and still is, a truly wonderful revolution | Barbi Marković

author: Lyndsey Winship
description:
Sadler’s Wells East, London
Ben Duke’s clever, witty and wholly unpredictable new show, The Last Hamlet, takes big liberties with the story that pay off

Hamlet is trying to get a hire car. He has missed his dad’s funeral because he was at a silent retreat, dealing with his abandonment issues and the disturbing memory of a year 7 disco when his uncle and mum danced together to Yazoo’s Only You.

There have been many takes on the troubled Prince of Denmark, but performer/director Ben Duke, co-founder of Lost Dog, has a talent for fresh readings. If Duke has a shtick – which after similar reworkings of Paradise Lost, Romeo and Juliet and the
title: This extraordinary new Hamlet turns Shakespeare inside out with infinite jest – and cuddly toys

author: Sarah Kopp
description:
At 15, having the cool 31-year-old PE teacher single me out felt thrilling. It took years to see his praise for what it really was

I was 15 when Paul joined my high school in Queensland, Australia, as a PE teacher. He was fun and handsome, and seemed much younger than his 31 years. I was obsessed with dance, and when Paul complimented me on my gymnastics, I was thrilled the “cool” teacher had noticed me.

He’d always stop for a chat. I was the only child of a single mum and though she was there for me, I didn’t confide in her. But he was easy to talk to and I quickly developed a crush.

Continue reading...
title: Experience: I helped jail the teacher who groomed me

author: Simon Hattenstone
description:
In 1986, Bamber was convicted of the murders of five members of his family. He has always protested his innocence. This year, with the help of leading experts, we have re-examined some of the most compelling evidence

  • Warning: this piece contains crime-scene photographs

The White House Farm massacre is one of Britain’s most notorious and horrifying crimes. On 7 August 1985, five members of the Bamber family were shot dead at their farmhouse in Essex, England. This Wednesday marked exactly 40 years since Jeremy Bamber was convicted of the murders of his adoptive parents, his sister and her six-year-old twin boys. He was initially jailed for a minimum of 25 years, later upgraded to a whole-life sentence.

If Bamber did kill his family, it is right that he remains in prison. But there have always been questions about the safety of his convictions, and these have grown recently. My late reporting partner, Eric Allison, formerly the prisons corresponden
title: The Jeremy Bamber files: three crucial questions about the White House Farm massacre

author: Harry Pearl
description:
Rescuers were unable to save the whales after they became beached on a remote and rocky part of the country

More than 40 pilot whales died after a mass stranding event on New Zealand’s remote east coast, conservation officials said on Friday, despite rescue efforts by volunteers and conservation workers.

The Department of Conservation (DoC) said 43 whales had died in the mass stranding along the Ngawi coast on the south-eastern tip of the North Island.

title: More than 40 pilot whales die after mass stranding in New Zealand’s North Island

Tennessee filing gives no reason for withdrawal over Bryan Seaver after estate secured restraining order against him

author: Agence France-Presse
description:
Three suitcases’ worth of the spiders were on their way to Germany, where they could fetch an estimated €1.5m

More than 3,000 tarantulas were seized at an airport in Lima on their way to Germany, Peruvian authorities said.

The spiders were hidden inside dirty socks contained in three suitcases carried by two Germans and a Polish citizen, the National Forestry and Wildlife Service (SERFOR) told Agence France-Presse on Thursday.

description:
